page.title: Virtual Conference Production Guide
page.description: Learn the key decisions, platform choices, staffing, timelines and replay steps for producing a virtual conference today.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual conference production?
page.definition: Virtual conference production is the end‑to‑end process of designing agenda architecture, selecting a streaming platform, coordinating backstage crew, managing live transitions, routing attendees between sessions, and delivering edited replays within two days and providing a run of show, speaker briefs, branded graphics, backup streams, and post‑event analytics.
page.quick_answer: Pick a platform that matches your audience size and interaction needs, then lock a run of show and schedule a full rehearsal at least two days before the live date. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: Which platform type fits my virtual conference?

blocks.p: Choose a self‑serve streaming studio for simple webinars or an enterprise event suite for multi‑track conferences. Three cost models exist: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars), self‑serve monthly plans (StreamYard, Livestorm), and annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast). Ten platforms compared below, from self‑serve streaming studios to enterprise event suites.

sections.h2: What goes into a run of show for a virtual conference?

blocks.p: A run of show lists every session, speaker cue, transition, and backup plan in chronological order.

sections.h2: Which production roles do I need for a virtual conference?

blocks.p: Staffing scales with complexity, from a single producer for a webinar to a full crew for a summit.

sections.h2: What is the typical timeline and lead time for a virtual conference?

blocks.p: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; a webinar needs three to four weeks. Lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. Schedule one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and a technical check 60 minutes before going live. Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event.

sections.h2: How do I manage replays, recordings and post‑event assets?

blocks.p: Capture a clean recording, edit branded clips, and publish the replay within one to two days.

faq.q: How do I choose between a self‑serve platform and an enterprise suite?
faq.a: Match the platform to session count, audience size, and interaction depth; self‑serve tools handle single‑track webinars with modest budgets, while enterprise suites provide multi‑track scheduling, networking lounges, and dedicated support for large summits and analytics dashboards for sponsor reporting in real time.

faq.q: What should a run of show include for a hybrid event?
faq.a: Include venue cue times, remote speaker hand‑offs, on‑site camera switches, audience polling triggers, and a fallback stream for each session so the online audience never loses the feed and a clear contact list for technical leads on both sides during the live day.

faq.q: How many rehearsals are needed before a virtual conference?
faq.a: Run one full rehearsal on the actual platform two to five days before the event, followed by a technical check sixty minutes before go‑live; additional dry runs are optional for complex multi‑track agendas to verify speaker audio, slide transitions, and backup stream activation.

faq.q: When should the replay be delivered to attendees?
faq.a: Publish the edited replay within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours after the live close, while the content is still fresh; include highlight clips, transcripts, and an analytics summary for sponsors and a download link for offline viewing to maximise post‑event engagement.
